extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), corporate counsel, investor relations and disclosure professionals preparing SEC periodic and registration filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory disclosure requirements from Regulation S-K (Items 104–106 and 201–202) covering mine safety, risk factors, cybersecurity, market/holder information, equity compensation, performance graphs, and descriptions of securities for SEC periodic and registration filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report all mine fatalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must report all fatalities occurring at a coal or other mine during the period covered by the report unless the fatality has been determined by MSHA to be unrelated to mining activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an absolute reporting requirement for the period covered. The exclusion applies only where MSHA has determined the fatality unrelated to mining activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: List mines receiving MSHA written notice of pattern or potential pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of coal or other mines, of which the registrant or a subsidiary of the registrant is an operator, that receive written notice from the Mine Safety and Health Administration of: (i) a pattern of violations of mandatory health or safety standards that are of such nature as could have significantly and substantially contributed to the cause and effect of coal or other mine health or safety hazards under section 104(e); or (ii) the potential to have such a pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mines operated by registrant or its subsidiaries that have received MSHA written notice either of an existing pattern of violations under 30 U.S.C. 814(e) or the potential to have such a pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report pending legal actions before Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Any pending legal action before the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission involving such coal or other mine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant must report the total number of legal actions pending before the Commission as of the last day of the reporting period, and the aggregate number instituted and resolved during the reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakdown of pending mine-safety legal actions by category
rubrics_metrics.description: For pending legal actions before the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission, report the number that are: (1) contests of citations and orders (Subpart B); (2) contests of proposed penalties (Subpart C); (3) complaints for compensation (Subpart D); (4) complaints of discharge, discrimination or interference (Subpart E); (5) applications for temporary relief (Subpart F); and (6) appeals of judges' decisions or orders to the Commission (Subpart H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts for each enumerated category as part of the total pending legal actions reported for the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions applicable to Item 104 (mine safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Item 104: (1) 'coal or other mine' means a coal or other mine as defined in section 3 of the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977 (30 U.S.C. 802) that is subject to the Act; (2) 'operator' has the meaning in section 3 of that Act; and (3) 'subsidiary' has the meaning given in Exchange Act Rule 12b-2 (17 CFR 240.12b-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the statutory and rule definitions when determining scope of reporting under Item 104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference and exhibit requirements for Item 104
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must provide the information required by this Item as specified by §229.601(b)(95). In addition, the registrant must provide a statement, in an appropriately captioned section of the periodic report, that the information concerning mine safety violations or other regulatory matters required by Section 1503(a) of the Dodd-Frank Act and this Item is included in exhibit 95 to the periodic report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the disclosure is included in an exhibit to an annual report on Form 10-K, the information is to be provided for the registrant's fiscal year. Follow §229.601(b)(95) placement and exhibit conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Factors: discuss material factors under caption 'Risk Factors'
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, provide under the caption 'Risk Factors' a discussion of the material factors that make an investment in the registrant or offering speculative or risky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discussion must be organized logically with relevant headings and each risk factor should be set forth under a subcaption that adequately describes the risk. Avoid presenting risks that are purely generic to any registrant; if such generic risks are presented, disclose them at the end of the risk factor section under the caption 'General Risk Factors.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Factors: concise explanation of how each risk affects the registrant
rubrics_metrics.description: Concisely explain how each risk affects the registrant or the securities being offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each risk must include a concise explanation of its effect on the company or securities rather than merely naming the risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Factors: summary requirement when discussion exceeds 15 pages
rubrics_metrics.description: If the risk factor discussion is longer than 15 pages, include in the forepart of the prospectus or annual report a series of concise, bulleted or numbered statements no more than two pages summarizing the principal factors that make an investment speculative or risky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the two-page summary in the forepart; ensure it summarizes principal risks concisely. If the risk factor discussion is in a registration statement, it must immediately follow the summary section required by §229.503; if no summary, it must follow the cover page or pricing information section as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Factors: plain English requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must furnish risk factor information in plain English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, straightforward language understandable to a reasonable investor. See §230.421(d) of Regulation C for related plain-English guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity definitions for Item 106
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'Cybersecurity incident' means an unauthorized occurrence, or series of related unauthorized occurrences, on or conducted through a registrant's information systems that jeopardizes confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the systems or information. 'Cybersecurity threat' means any potential unauthorized occurrence that may result in adverse effects on confidentiality, integrity, or availability. 'Information systems' means electronic information resources owned or used by the registrant, including physical or virtual infrastructure or components organized for collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of the registrant's information to maintain or support operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these definitions throughout Item 106 disclosures to determine what events, systems, and risks must be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity risk management and strategy disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the registrant's processes, if any, for assessing, identifying, and managing material risks from cybersecurity threats in sufficient detail for a reasonable investor to understand those processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address, as applicable: (i) whether/how such processes are integrated into overall risk management; (ii) whether the registrant engages assessors, consultants, auditors, or other third parties in connection with such processes; and (iii) whether the registrant has processes to oversee and identify cybersecurity risks associated with its use of any third-party service provider. The list is non-exclusive; provide sufficient detail for investor understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity: disclose material effects of cyber risks or incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe whether any risks from cybersecurity threats, including as a result of any previous cybersecurity incidents, have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect the registrant, including its business strategy, results of operations, or financial condition and if so, how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material impacts have occurred or are reasonably likely, provide narrative explanation of how strategy, operations, or financials were or may be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity governance disclosure (board oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the board of directors' oversight of risks from cybersecurity threats. If applicable, identify any board committee or subcommittee responsible for oversight and describe the processes by which the board or such committee is informed about such risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether oversight is performed by full board or a committee, name the committee if applicable, and explain the information flows and processes used to keep the board/committee informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity management roles and expertise disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe management's role in assessing and managing the registrant's material risks from cybersecurity threats, including whether and which management positions or committees are responsible and the relevant expertise of such persons or members in such detail as necessary to fully describe the nature of the expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address which management positions/committees are responsible, provide relevant expertise examples (e.g., prior work experience, degrees, certifications), describe processes by which such persons monitor prevention, detection, mitigation, and remediation, and indicate whether they report to the board or a board committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity governance instruction for foreign private issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction: In the case of a foreign private issuer with a two-tier board, for purposes of Item 106(c) the term 'board of directors' means the supervisory or non-management board. For certain foreign private issuers meeting §240.10A-3(c)(3), it means board of auditors or statutory auditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the issuer-appropriate board equivalent when preparing board oversight disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured Data Requirement for Item 106
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the information required by this Item in an Interactive Data File in accordance with Rule 405 of Regulation S-T and the EDGAR Filer Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 106 requires structured-data (interactive) submission; follow Rule 405 Reg S-T and EDGAR Filer Manual formatting and filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market information: principal market(s) and trading symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the principal United States market(s) and the corresponding trading symbol(s) for each class of the registrant's common equity. For foreign registrants, also identify the principal foreign public trading market(s), if any, and corresponding trading symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear identification of markets and symbols for each class of common equity registered under Section 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market information: OTC market disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the principal United States market for such common equity is not an exchange, indicate that any over-the-counter market quotations reflect inter-dealer prices, without retail mark-up, mark-down or commission and may not necessarily represent actual transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the nature and limitations of OTC quotations if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market information when no established public trading market exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is no established public trading market for a class of common equity, furnish a statement to that effect and, if applicable, state the range of high and low bid information for each full quarterly period within the two most recent fiscal years and any subsequent interim period for which financial statements are included, indicating the source of such quotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to quotations must be qualified by appropriate explanation. Limited or sporadic quotations should not of themselves be deemed an 'established public trading market.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure in registration statements for classes without US market
rubrics_metrics.description: If the information called for is being presented in a registration statement on Form S-1 or Form 10 relating to a class of common equity for which at the time of filing there is no established U.S. public trading market, indicate the amount(s) of common equity: (ii) that could be sold pursuant to §230.144 or that the registrant has agreed to register under the Securities Act for sale by security holders; or (iii) that is being, or has been publicly proposed to be, publicly offered by the registrant (unless pursuant to an employee benefit plan or dividend reinvestment plan), the offering of which could have a material effect on the market price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose equity amounts that could materially affect market price under the specified categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holders: approximate number and transactional effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Set forth the approximate number of holders of each class of common equity as of the latest practicable date. If presented in a registration or proxy related to an acquisition, indicate the effect of the transaction on the amount and percentage of present holdings beneficially owned by any person known to the registrant to be the beneficial owner of more than five percent of any class, each director and nominee, and all directors and officers as a group, and the registrant's present commitments to such persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the approximate holder counts and, where relevant to transactions, detailed effects on ownership percentages and commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dividends disclosure and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where registrants have a record of paying no cash dividends although earnings indicate an ability to do so, they are encouraged to consider stating their intention to pay cash dividends in the foreseeable future; registrants with a history of paying cash dividends are encouraged to indicate whether they currently expect comparable cash dividends to continue and, if not, the nature of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are encouraged disclosures to inform investors about dividend policy and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity compensation plan tabular disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide, in the specified tabular format, information as of the end of the most recently completed fiscal year for compensation plans under which equity securities are authorized for issuance, aggregated as: (i) all compensation plans previously approved by security holders; and (ii) all compensation plans not previously approved by security holders. The table shall include: number of securities to be issued upon exercise of outstanding options, warrants and rights; weighted-average exercise price of outstanding options, warrants and rights; and number of securities remaining available for future issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact tabular columns and aggregation categories. For each category include the (a) number of securities issuable upon exercise of outstanding options/warrants/rights; (b) weighted-average exercise price; and (c) number remaining available for future issuance. Follow formatting shown in Item 201(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity compensation: narrative disclosure for non-approved plans
rubrics_metrics.description: For each compensation plan under which equity securities are authorized for issuance that was adopted without the approval of security holders, describe briefly, in narrative form, the material features of the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise narrative descriptions of material features for any non-shareholder-approved plans or individual arrangements as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity compensation disclosure scope and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure shall be provided with respect to any compensation plan and individual compensation arrangement (including parent, subsidiary, affiliate plans) under which equity securities are authorized for issuance to employees or non-employees. No disclosure required for (a) any plan, contract or arrangement for issuance of warrants or rights to all security holders pro rata, or (b) any employee benefit plan intended to meet Section 401(a) qualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'individual compensation arrangement' includes written compensation contracts and plans applicable to one person. Registrants may aggregate plan information for classes of securities and may aggregate information regarding individual arrangements with plan information as applicable. Provide footnotes where aggregation includes other types of arrangements and disclose formulas that automatically increase available securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity compensation: special footnote and aggregation instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number remaining available for future issuance includes securities available under any compensation plan or individual arrangement other than upon exercise of an option/warrant/right, disclose the number and type of plan separately for each such plan in a footnote. If an equity compensation plan contains a formula for calculating available securities, disclose the formula in a footnote to the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide aggregate disclosure but add footnotes to break out non-standard availability and formula-based increases. Cross-references to financial-statement descriptions may satisfy narrative requirements where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance graph: required comparisons and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a line graph comparing yearly percentage change in the registrant's cumulative total shareholder return on a class of common stock with: (i) the cumulative total return of a broad equity market index (or S&P 500 if registrant is within that index); and (ii) cumulative total return of either (A) a published industry/line-of-business index, (B) peer issuer(s) selected in good faith (disclose basis), or (C) issuer(s) with similar market capitalizations (only if not using a published industry index and cannot reasonably identify a peer group; explain reasons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one of the alternatives in (ii); if constructing a peer group index, use the same methodology for registrant and peer index. Disclose identity of peer issuers and bases for selection where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance graph: measurement period and plotting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement period begins at the 'measurement point' (market close on the last trading day before the beginning of the registrant's fifth preceding fiscal year) through the end of the registrant's last completed fiscal year. The registrant is required to present information for the last five fiscal years (may graph a longer period but the measurement point remains).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In preparing graphic comparisons, use comparable methods and assumptions for total return calculations, assume reinvestment of dividends, convert closing price at the measurement point into a fixed investment in dollars, plot cumulative returns for each fiscal year, and weight component issuers by market capitalization at the beginning of each period. Smaller reporting companies are exempt from paragraph (e). If index selection changes, explain reason(s) and compare returns with both new and prior indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 202 Capital stock disclosure elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If capital stock is to be registered, state the title of the class and describe relevant matters listed, including: dividend rights; terms of conversion; sinking fund provisions; redemption provisions; voting rights (including vote required to take action); any Board classification and its impact where cumulative voting permitted; liquidation rights; preemption rights; liability to further calls or assessment by registrant for liabilities imposed on stockholders; any restriction on alienability; and any provision discriminating against holders owning a substantial amount of securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the items (a)(1)(i)-(xi) as applicable. No complete legal description required, but give sufficient information for investors to understand rights and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of rights without majority vote
rubrics_metrics.description: If the rights of holders of such stock may be modified otherwise than by a vote of a majority or more of the shares outstanding, voting as a class, so state and explain briefly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any special modification mechanisms or supermajority/other terms that alter how rights can be changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred stock repurchase/redeem restriction disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If preferred stock is to be registered, describe briefly any restriction on the repurchase or redemption of shares by the registrant while there is any arrearage in the payment of dividends or sinking fund installments; if none, so state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State presence or absence of restrictions on repurchase/redemption tied to arrearage in payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of rights limited by another authorized class
rubrics_metrics.description: If the rights evidenced by, or amounts payable with respect to, the shares to be registered are, or may be, materially limited or qualified by the rights of any other authorized class of securities, include information regarding such other securities sufficient to enable investors to understand such limitations or qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cross-referenced or direct disclosure of other classes when they materially limit rights of the class being registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of provisions delaying or preventing change in control
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe briefly or cross-reference any provision of the registrant's charter or by-laws that would have an effect of delaying, deferring or preventing a change in control of the registrant and that would operate only with respect to an extraordinary corporate transaction (e.g., merger, reorganization, tender offer, sale or transfer of substantially all assets, or liquidation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude provisions required by law or governmental/judicial authority and arrangements adopted solely to effect compliance with law unless such compliance required the specific provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt securities disclosure elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If debt securities are to be registered, state the title, principal amount offered (and if a series, total amount authorized and total amount outstanding) and describe relevant matters as applicable: provisions regarding maturity, interest, conversion, redemption, amortization, sinking fund or retirement; lien provisions and identification of properties subject to lien; subordination and aggregate amount of outstanding senior indebtedness where designated subordinated; restrictions on dividends or asset ratios or reserves; restrictions on incurrence of additional debt; events constituting default and periodic evidence requirements; modification provisions; original issue discount tax effects; and trustee name, material relationships, percentage to require trustee action, and indemnification the trustee may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the specific elements listed in paragraph (b)(1)-(10) as applicable to the debt securities being registered; omit complete legal descriptions but include sufficient investor-relevant terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warrants and rights disclosure elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities are to be offered pursuant to warrants or rights state: the amount of securities called for by such warrants or rights; the period during which and the price at which the warrants or rights are exercisable; the amount of warrants or rights outstanding; provisions for changes to or adjustments in the exercise price; and any other material terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear terms for warrants and rights comparable to the capital stock and debt disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other securities: brief comparable description
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities other than capital stock, debt, warrants or rights are to be registered, include a brief description (comparable to that required in paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of Item 202) of the rights evidenced thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a succinct description of rights and terms sufficient for investor understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market information for securities other than common equity
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities other than common equity are to be registered and there is an established public trading market for such securities, provide market information with respect to such securities comparable to that required by paragraph (a) of Item 201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply market and trading-symbol information, or state absence of established market and provide bid/range data as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) disclosure elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If Depositary Shares represented by American Depositary Receipts are being registered, furnish: (1) the name of the depositary and address of its principal executive office; (2) the title of the ADRs and identification of the deposited security and a brief description of the terms of deposit, including the amount of deposited securities represented by one unit; voting procedures; collection/distribution of dividends; transmission of notices/reports/proxy materials; sale/exercise of rights; deposit/sale of securities from dividends, splits or reorganizations; amendment/extension/termination of the deposit; rights of holders to inspect transfer books and lists of holders; restrictions on deposit/withdrawal; limitation on depositary liability; and (3) describe all fees and charges which may be imposed directly or indirectly against the holder of the ADRs, indicating the type of service, amount of fee or charges and to whom paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exhaustive ADR mechanics and fee disclosures as listed in Item 202(f)(1)-(3) to inform holders of rights and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 202 instructions: information of type and general character
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever the title of securities is required, provide information indicating the type and general character of the securities: for shares, par/stated value, dividend rate and preference, conversion/redeemable status; for debt, rate of interest, date of maturity, serial maturities, contingency and priority, convertibility/callability; for other securities, appropriate comparable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant is a foreign registrant, include limitations on nonresident ownership or voting, laws affecting remittance of dividends and other payments, taxes including withholding to which U.S. holders are subject, and description of reciprocal tax treaties or state absence thereof.
